messages.author: 3033a60610caec0b
messages.subject: Removing "layers"
parts:
I'm curious if one is able to remove layers from a ggplot object. My
case is as follows. I have done an awful lot of automated plot
creation, and have saved all ggplot objects to RData files. Later on,
I can revisit the plots and utilize the fact that the object is self
contained. My question is, can I remove a layer? Specifically in the
automated process I used levels of factor "a" to specify "linetype",
but would like to go back and facet based on factor "a" and have a
single "linetype". Is this possible?

Thanks,
Brandon

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Removing "layers"
parts:
Hi Brandon,

It's not really possible (although you can dig around in p$layers and
do it yourself) - I have thought about it, but haven't figured out the
right interface yet.

Hadley

messages.author: 3033a60610caec0b
messages.subject: Re: Removing "layers"
parts:
Hadley,

As always, thanks for the quick reply. As often happens, after posting
question digging around becomes much more fruitful. I determined that
if I call:

p$layers[[i]] <- NULL

I can remove the un-needed layer, and can then start to rebuild. Not a
process I would want to automate, as it isn't clear without inspection
what each layer does, but this works for custom charting.

Thanks for such a great package,
Brandon
